newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechnya plans museum of ex-leader Dudayev - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Chechnya plans museum of ex-leader Dudayev - Tass.

text.p: Chechnya plans to open a museum honouring Dzhokhar Dudayev, the man who led the region's bloody independence struggle against Russia, Itar-Tass news agency said on Monday.

Dudayev, who was reported killed in April 1996, was elected Chechnya's president in 1991. He spearheaded the region's resistance against Moscow when President Boris Yeltsin sent in troops two years ago to crush its independence bid.
The new museum will display Dudayev's traditional Chechen fur hat, his ornate military uniforms bearing Chechen emblems and other memorabilia, Tass said.

Estonia also has a museum honouring Dudayev, who is revered in the Baltic republic for his refusal while serving there as a Soviet air base commander in the late 1980s to halt its drive for independence from Moscow.
Riga, capital of neighbouring Latvia, renamed a city street after Dudayev earlier this year.
On Monday the Chechen parliament posthumously awarded Dudayev the title "generalissimo", Tass said.
Under a recent peace deal Russia plans to withdraw its last remaining troops from Chechnya before planned presidential and parliamentary elections there on January 27.
The accord, signed on August 31, defers the region's final political status for five years.
